doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: Black Pete, Cock-Eye George and the first paid job
summary: Reminiscence of Black Pete and Cock-Eye George, who took Willie on his first paid job, then playing at George Delcy's place.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You had to remember Did you know Black Pete? Yeah, he played piano.
That's right. I remember playing with him.
He knew Cock-Eye George because he took me on a job with Cock-Eye George.
You know Cock-Eye George? I was trying to make somebody know Cock-Eye George.

Yeah, well that's my first job. He took me on. I was playing the violin. And he took me on a job for the butcher where he used to buy meat. Pete in the Padres Market. You knew Pete. Sure. Well we played for him. He lived around Scott and Canal.
You know, he was a great big white fella.
Yeah, and we played. He took me on my first job where I made some money. I was in my teens.
Then you just told me, why, why, in 1918 you, why I had my teeth fish. Uh-huh. What'd you say? I said you played with me when I used to have my teeth fish.
You mean? No. Yeah, but I didn't play with him. He was playing without teeth down at, uh, down at the, uh, George Delcy there.
Yeah, yeah, you used to play with me when I got my teeth fish. I didn't call a right man George Delcy.
Well, George Delcy used to run the managing plays.
It was George Delcy, it was George Delcy's place. It was old man Anthony's son-in-law. Oh, it was his place? And we opened it up. Me, Chris Bond, and Peter Burkage. Opened that place up.
